CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA

ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Smt.Suma K., learned counsel for the appellants and Sri.G.S.Marulaiah, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.
The adequacy of compensation granted is questioned in this appeal by the claimants.
The order under challenge is the one which is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysuru in MVC.No.138/2018 dated 29.11.2021.

As borne by record, appellant No.1 in the capacity of mother, appellant No.2 in the capacity of father of a 12 years old boy by name Master Chethan who died in a road traffic accident, filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.3,30,000/- as compensation.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the following second schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal assessed compensation and granted a meager sum, which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel states that income of the deceased Master Chethan is required to be taken notionally as Rs.30,000/- per annum, however, the Tribunal did not do so.

In this regard, learned counsel relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MEENA DEVI VS. NUNU CHAND MAHTO @ NEMCHAND MAHTO & ORS.1 (2023) 1 SCC 204 [Arising out of SLP (C)
No.5345/2019) NC: 2024:KHC:32432 Meenakshi vs Sanna Ningamma on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133887505/
2 5.

entities.text: MEENA DEVI VS. NUNU CHAND MAHTO @ NEMCHAND MAHTO & ORS.1 (2023) 1 SCC 204
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said decision dealing with a matter where a 12 years old boy met with an accident and lost his life, the Hon'ble Supreme Court at para No.16 of the order held as follows:
"16.

Thus applying the ratio of the said judgments, looking to the age of the child in the present case i.e. 12 years, the principles laid down in Kishan Gopal [Kishan Gopal v. Lala, (2014) 1 SCC 244 : (2014) 1 SCC (Civ) 184 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri) 241] are aptly applicable to the facts of the present case.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal [Kishan Gopal v. Lala, (2014) 1 SCC 244 : (2014) 1 SCC (Civ) 184 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri) 241]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the ocular statement of the mother of the deceased, it is clear that the deceased was a brilliant student and studying in a private school.

Therefore, accepting the notional earning Rs 30,000 including future prospect and applying the multiplier of 15 in view of the decision of this Court in Sarla Verma [Sarla Verma v. DTC, (2009) 6 SCC 121 :
(2009) 2 SCC (Civ) 770 : (2009) 2 SCC (Cri) 1002] , the loss of dependency comes to Rs 4,50,000 and if we add Rs 50,000 in conventional heads, then the total sum of compensation comes to Rs 5,00,000.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma [Sarla Verma v. DTC, (2009) 6 SCC 121 :
(2009) 2 SCC (Civ) 770 : (2009) 2 SCC (Cri) 1002]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the judgment of MACT, lump sum compensation of Rs 1,50,000 has been awarded, while the High Court enhanced it to Rs.2,00,000 up to the value of the claim petition.
In our view, the said amount of compensation is not just and reasonable looking to the computation made hereinabove.

Hence, we determine the total compensation as Rs.5,00,000 and on reducing the amount as awarded by NC: 2024:KHC:32432 the High Court i.e. Rs 2,00,000, the enhanced amount comes to Rs 3,00,000."
6.
Learned counsel ultimately seeks the Court to apply the analogy in the aforementioned judgment and pass orders accordingly.
7. Sri.G.S.Marulaiah, learned counsel for respondent No.2 based his submission relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of KISHAN GOPAL AND ANOTHER VS. LALA AND OTHERS2.

entities.text: KISHAN GOPAL AND ANOTHER VS. LALA AND OTHERS2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said case, the Hon'ble Apex Court at para No.39 of the judgment held as under:
"39.

In view of the aforesaid reasons, it would be just and reasonable for us to take his notional income at Rs 30,000 and further taking the young age of the parents,
namely, the mother who was about 36 years old, at the time of accident, by applying the legal principles laid down in Sarla Verma v. DTC [(2009) 6 SCC 121 :
(2009) 2 SCC (Civ) 770 : (2009) 2 SCC (Cri) 1002] , the multiplier of 15 can be applied to the multiplicand.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v. DTC [(2009) 6 SCC 121 :
(2009) 2 SCC (Civ) 770 : (2009) 2 SCC (Cri) 1002]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, 30,000  15 = 4,50,000 and 50,000 under conventional heads towards loss of love and affection, funeral (2014) 1 SCC 244 NC:

2024:KHC:32432 expenses, last rites as held in Kerala SRTC v. Susamma Thomas [(1994) 2 SCC 176 : 1994 SCC (Cri) 335] , which is referred to in Lata Wadhwa case [Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar, (2001) 8 SCC 197] and the said amount under the conventional heads is awarded even in relation to the death of children between 10 to 15 years old.

entities.text: Kerala SRTC v. Susamma Thomas [(1994) 2 SCC 176 : 1994 SCC (Cri) 335]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar, (2001) 8 SCC 197
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case also we award Rs 50,000 under conventional heads.

In our Meenakshi vs Sanna Ningamma on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133887505/
3 view, for the aforesaid reasons the said amount would be fair, just and reasonable compensation to be awarded in favour of the appellants."

entities.text: Meenakshi vs Sanna Ningamma on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Both the aforementioned decisions make it clear that notional income has to be taken as Rs.30,000/- per year.
It is not in dispute that the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '15'.

Thus,
'loss of dependancy' comes to Rs.4,50,000/-.
Also, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is required to be added under 'other conventional heads'.
Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to would be Rs.5,00,000/-.
Thus, this Court is of the view that the appeal is required to be allowed in part.

Therefore, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2024:KHC:32432 ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mysuru through orders in MVC.No.138/2018 dated 29.11.2021 is enhanced from Rs.3,30,000/- to Rs.5,00,000/-.
iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v) On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE NR/-
